name: HEARTS Capsule Hotel & Spa HAKATA
detail: Fukuoka Airport is close to Hakata Station, and the hotel is also near the station. There are pajamas and basic amenities provided, and the capsule is reasonably spacious with a TV, charging outlets, and a mirror, so it's comfortable. There are lockers for valuables, and it's convenient as you can access the hot spring bath from there. I enjoyed delicious bread at Dakomekka, which is very close to the hotel. The staff at the reception were friendly, and I felt safe staying in the women-only floor.

name: UNPLAN Fukuoka
detail: There is Ohori Park right nearby, making it great for walks. A simple breakfast is offered, and near the park are the Fukuoka City Art Museum, a museum, and a botanical and zoological garden. It is also close to Hakata Station, Nakasu, and Tenjin, and there are shared bicycles right next to the entrance, which is very convenient. The lounge tables have plenty of electrical sockets, outlets, and USB ports, so there was no inconvenience using them. The lobby on the 5th floor is always accessible, and there are coin-operated washers and dryers, making laundry easy. It is excellent in terms of cost-effectiveness.

name: APA Hotel Fukuoka Tenjinnishi
detail: The location was easily accessible on foot and convenient for shopping. The accommodation had good hot water supply and the bathroom was clean, allowing for a pleasant stay. The housekeeping service was also very satisfactory. The staff's attitude was friendly, and the overall facilities were well-equipped, making for a comfortable time.

name: THE LIVELY FUKUOKA HAKATA
detail: The location was good and transportation was convenient, and the overall cleanliness of the accommodation was neat. The room size was decent, and the bathroom and hot water usage were satisfactory, making it comfortable to stay. The basic amenities were well provided, and the satisfaction level was fairly good for the price. The staff were generally friendly, but their responsiveness was not very impressive, and the view was somewhat disappointing.

name: 9h nine hours Hakata station
detail: The Sleep Pod is specialized for sleeping. It's quiet and comfortable. I was impressed by the enveloping pillows. There is no TV or radio. There are USB and regular outlets available. It supports multiple languages, and the pictogram design is stylish. You can use a card key for both the elevator and lockers (the timing for scanning the locker QR code is a bit tricky). Organizing luggage in the lockers was somewhat difficult. You can eat and drink in the 9th-floor co-ed lounge. It's spacious, and of course, there’s free Wi-Fi, and a co-working space where you can work adequately. I opted for a breakfast included plan, which can be enjoyed at a fast-food restaurant behind the hotel. I chose a rice burger and miso soup. It was very delicious. Since each meal is over 1000 yen, the breakfast plan feels like a better deal. Amenities (toothbrushes and basic skincare products) are sold in vending machines within the hotel. There are several convenience stores nearby, so it was convenient. Very...

name: Hotel Forza Hakataeki Chikushi-Guchi I
detail: Since it was a trip with my mom, convenience was our top priority. The Forza Hotel was truly the best since it's just a stone's throw from Hakata Station. The transportation facilities are excellent, and you can quickly reach anywhere and find your way around. Since my mom is elderly, we requested breakfast for all three nights. The breakfast was clean and tasted decent, but the menu was the same throughout our three nights, haha. If you're expecting a variety for breakfast, it might not meet those expectations! However, it's important for older adults to have a hearty breakfast, so it might not be a bad option. My mom was a bit confused by the same menu but didn't have any major complaints, haha. The miso soup and rice were tasty, and there was something like beef that was also delicious. I had the salad and karaage together, and it was really good, but I couldn't eat it every day, haha. Nonetheless, putting all that aside, I was very satisfied because the transportation was convenient and the accessibility to nearby attractions was excellent. The staff were very friendly, and the employee who was fluent in Korean was truly outstanding. Taking a bus in Fukuoka is very easy, and the airport direct bus stop is right in front of the hotel, really. You don't even need to cross the road, it's right in front of the hotel! Truly the best of the best! Since I stayed from Monday to Wednesday, the accommodation cost wasn't too high and was about 20, so I think it's more than sufficient for a place right in front of Hakata Station, haha. You can also store your luggage for free before check-in! There's a large supermarket just a 5-minute walk away! The Don Quijote Minami store is also about an 8-minute bus ride away, and the bus fare is 210 yen! Taking the bus is really easy and quick! Tochoji Temple is just one stop away by subway! It's a 6-minute walk from Tochoji to Kushida Shrine. You can ride the bus from Kushida Shrine for just two stops back to Hakata Station! Everything was really convenient and great, haha. I highly recommend Forza Hotel for those traveling by foot who have a lot of sightseeing planned! There was a slight odor in the hallway, but it's not like we were sleeping in the hallway, right?ㅠㅠ hahaha. I was very satisfied! I had a great stay for three days^^!! Thank you~~~!!!!

name: Epoch inn Nakasu
detail: The location behind Don Quijote in Nakasu is superb. I was initially worried about the unmanned hotel, but I was able to connect to the front desk through the tablet at the entrance and check in smoothly. The facilities were new and felt clean. The downside was that the large TV was facing the narrow side of the room, making it a bit difficult to see.

name: WeBase HAKATA Hostel
detail: I used a 4-person room with bunk beds. The room was very clean. The shower room and powder room were also hygienic. Breakfast included bread, jam, yogurt, cereal, milk, coffee, and juice. It takes about a 20-minute walk to Marine Messe. I'm very satisfied with the price and everything. One point: I requested earplugs and room wear at the front desk to be left in my room, but they weren't there. However, I was able to sleep soundly. I will stay here again during the next live event.

name: APA Hotel Hakataeki Chikushiguchi
detail: [Advantages and Recommendations] Best cost-performance and accessibility: It is located very close to the station, making it highly accessible and offering great performance for the price. It is the perfect choice for travelers who primarily just sleep at the accommodation and go through their travel itinerary. Public bath facilities: The hotel has a large public bath, which is great for relieving fatigue after a day of activities. If you visit, I highly recommend using it. (However, there are three Apa Hotels in close proximity, so make sure you confirm you are entering the correct building that you booked to avoid confusion.) Foreign language services: There are staff who speak English available at check-in, so there were no communication issues, and at checkout, there was also staff who spoke Korean, which was convenient. [Disadvantages and Usage Tips] Small room and bathroom size: The room and bathroom are quite small. The hotel advises storing luggage under the bed, but it is troublesome to constantly fold and unfold it, and I felt uneasy about the space under the bed, so I kept my luggage laid out horizontally in the hallway by the door. Even so, the space for movement remains minimal. Hygiene status: The floor is carpeted and tends to collect some dust, so I didn’t feel that the room was very clean. For those who are not overly sensitive about hygiene, it is sufficient for just sleeping. [Overall Review] While the small room size and imperfect hygiene are somewhat disappointing, the strong advantages of accessibility, cost-performance, and the public bath make it a place I return to each time I visit Japan. I recommend it for those who want a practical travel experience.

name: The Millennials Fukuoka
detail: The room had one double bed with a reclining function, and it had a decent ceiling height as well as width. Despite being a capsule hotel, the space felt spacious. The facility was generally clean, and there was a complete separation of areas for men and women, with a security key system in place at the entrance door of the area, ensuring safety and security. There were free bar (free drink) sessions held twice, once in the evening and once at night. Despite being free, the staff made each drink individually, and they tasted quite sophisticated and delicious. I would definitely like to use this place again if the opportunity arises!
